findings.claim: The first-wave residual is carried almost entirely by turns with an enemy knight adjacent to the queen (within 60), not by the wave's size, the merges, or how she kites: lost races have 3.1 more adjacent turns and lose about 1.9 HP per adjacent turn.
findings.numbers: v12 Gold, 115 HP races (42 lost / 73 won, summary.csv + per-game traces): k500AtContact 3.50 vs 3.38 (MW p=0.36), hpK500AtContact 47.4 vs 43.2 (p=0.11), spawned20 3.7 vs 4.1 (p=0.91); lossK20 10.24 vs 3.42 (bootstrap diff +6.8 HP, 95% CI +3.7..+10.3); adjacent turns (nearest knight <=60 in the 20-turn window) 5.17 vs 2.07 (CI +1.6..+4.7); 39/73 won races have 0 adjacent turns vs 8/42 lost; OLS lossK20 = 1.88 x adjTurns, R2 0.89 (115 races); loss per threatened turn 0.75 vs 0.31 HP (CI +0.23..+0.66): the intensity part of the 6.8-HP gap is 5.2 HP, the duration part 0.75. Kiting/standing metrics identical: moves20 10.1 vs 10.3, meanMove20 62.6 vs 62.2, meanNearTower20 120 vs 118, topups20 5.3 vs 5.4, stuckMoves20 0.02 vs 0.00.
findings.evidence: q1_compare.py -> q1-v12.txt (lost vs won races tables), q3_control.py -> q3-v12.txt (loss per threatened turn decomposition), q8_robust.py -> q8-v12.txt (lossK20 ~ adjTurns). Observation.

findings.claim: The knights stay adjacent because our towers kill them too slowly at the contact: in lost races the enemy wave arrives about 3 turns earlier, before our second tower is up, so the queen fights it with one tower (and a 196-HP tower built under the wave). Tower damage is set by tower HP (range), one target per tower per turn, so the count alone is not the lever; the second tower's timing relative to the contact is a strong gradient.
findings.numbers: towersAtContact 1.43 vs 1.75 (MW p=0.017; one tower in 22/42 lost vs 25/73 won), towerHpAtContact 887 vs 1070 (CI -341..-32), coverQAtContact 1.40 vs 1.70 (p=0.022); contact turn 24.5 vs 27.3 (p=0.021) while the 2nd tower completes at turn 25 in both groups (25.2 vs 24.9, p=0.73; DeathTrace ours); 2nd tower at/after the contact in 31/42 lost vs 35/73 won. Gradient over 115 races by (2nd tower turn - contact): <=-3: lossK20 1.1, 24% lost (n=21); [-3,0): 2.7, 21% (n=28); [0,3): 6.9, 36% (n=39); >=3: 11.6, 63% (n=27). Over all 176 games with a contact the win rate by the same bands: 21/34 (0.62), 36/47 (0.77), 32/56 (0.57), 16/39 (0.41). Kill-speed proxy ttk = waveHP / sum(3 + hp//200): 6.85 vs 5.38 (p=0.017); lossK20 by ttk band: <4: 1.1 HP (n=37, 0.5 adjacent turns); 4-6: 3.6 (32); 6-8: 6.3 (16); 8-12: 13.8 (22, 7.5 adjacent turns). ttk explains 43% of the variance in adjacent turns and 1.44 of the 3.1-turn adjacency gap. Total tower damage over the window is the same (dmgK20 76 vs 79, killK20 5.55 vs 5.84) but per threatened turn 7.0 vs 9.5 damage and 0.53 vs 0.75 kills; recorded damage per turn in the first 10 turns 5.06 vs 5.59 (p=0.06). Within the one-tower regime (24 lost / 25 won): first tower HP equal (652 vs 672), the new tower completes 3.5 vs 2.2 turns after the contact (p=0.008), walk turns to its site under knights 2.9 vs 1.7 (p=0.009), wave HP 52 vs 45 (p=0.09), adjacent turns 7.9 vs 4.2.
findings.evidence: q6_mech.py -> q6-v12.txt section (3), q7_levers.py -> q7-v12.txt (kill speed, t2rel bands), q8_robust.py -> q8-v12.txt, q9_onetower.py output; formula in W/src/main/java/cr/core/Rules.java:355 (damage = TOWER_CREEP_DAMAGE_MIN 3 + (range - dist)/200, range = sqrt((hp*1000 + siteArea)/pi), closest creep only) and Const.java:15-18. The association is observation (high confidence); the causal reading kill speed -> adjacency -> loss is inference (medium confidence).

findings.claim: The contact turn is the opponent's barracks timing, not our position: early-barracks opponents (first barracks by turn 8) meet our queen at turn 22 with 1.2 towers and we score only 50% against them; late-barracks opponents are the death lens, not the race lens.
findings.numbers: corr(contact turn, opponent firstBarracks) = 0.77 over 115 races; corr(contact, our distance from the back edge) = 0.26; our distance at contact no longer differs (322 vs 324, p=0.89; v11 444 vs 380). By opponent firstBarracks over all 180 games: <=8: 42 games, won 21/42 (0.50), contact 22.5, towersAtContact 1.24, our HP minus theirs at t50 -2.0, 15 of 33 races lost, 6 deaths; 9-12: 54 games, 35/54 (0.65), contact 25.3, towers 1.61, +4.4, 15/43 races lost; 13+: 82 games, 51/82 (0.62), contact 30.9, towers 1.96, +12.9, 12/39 races lost but 19 queen deaths (23%). Mean contact by opponent barracks turn: 1-5 -> 18-20, 7-8 -> 24-26, 13-16 -> 27-28, 18-19 -> 29-30.
findings.evidence: q7_levers.py -> q7-v12.txt (early rush section), q6-v12.txt (contact drivers), features-v12-gold.csv opp rows. Observation.

findings.claim: Our behaviour during the wave differs only in forward movement and walking to a new tower site under knights; most of the forward-move signal is a symptom of adjacency, and the kite rule's tower pull is not the cause. The net controllable part of the window behaviour is about 1-2 HP of the 6.8-HP gap.
findings.numbers: Forward moves under threat 4.19 vs 1.96 per game (CI +1.2..+3.3; AUC 0.72): forward kite MOVEs 2.93 vs 1.60 (p=0.002), forward walks to a new tower (BUILD on a not-yet-built site) 1.12 vs 0.30 (p<0.001), forward top-up walks 0.14 vs 0.05; backward moves equal (5.6 vs 6.0). Pooled over 176 games, HP lost on the turn after a move by nearest-knight band: knight at 0-60: forward 1.31 (n=275) vs backward 1.18 (n=261) - no direction effect when already adjacent; 121-180: forward 0.44 (n=88) vs back 0.11 (n=284); 181-250: forward 0.51 (n=81) vs back 0.02 (n=369). Forward moves with the knight >120 away: 1.14 vs 0.88 per game (p=0.07), costing 0.74 vs 0.26 HP per game (CI +0.15..+0.81). Forward kite MOVEs that approach her nearest tower: 0.12 vs 0.12 per game (p=0.87) - the pull is not it. Standing with a knight within 155: 0.52 vs 0.18 turns/game (p=0.10; k500=4 stratum 0.83 vs 0.18, p=0.027); stand/BUILD top-up turns with a knight <=100 cost 1.6-3.0 HP next turn (n=5-6 per class). OLS on lossK20 (ALL model, R2 0.75): fwdMoves20 contributes +2.5 HP and standReach20 +1.0 HP of the gap, but with adjTurns in the model fwdMoves20's coefficient falls from +2.14 to +0.11 (R2 0.91). Shapley R2 shares: opponent-set variables 0.12, our pre-contact choices 0.26, our in-window behaviour 0.38.
findings.evidence: q6_mech.py -> q6-v12.txt section (2), q3_control.py -> q3-v12.txt, q7-v12.txt (fwdFar, fwdMoveToTower), q8-v12.txt. Observation plus inference on endogeneity.

findings.claim: Merged waves still amplify the loss but no longer separate lost from won races in v12; the summary.csv column spawned20 is not the study's merge definition.
findings.numbers: Study definition (a turn with a knight within 250 followed by >=2 new knights within 500, net of kills): 17/42 lost vs 18/73 won; simple definition 12/42 vs 12/73 (the README's 12 of 42). Loss from the merge turn on 12.9 HP vs 5.3; before the merge 3.4 vs 0.8; unmerged races still lose 6.1 vs 2.5. spawned20>0 in 35/42 vs 61/73 (any spawn in the window). v11: 19/44 vs 7/62 (study).
findings.evidence: q6_mech.py -> q6-v12.txt section (1); q1-v12.txt (spawned20). Observation; medium-high confidence (the definition had to be reconstructed from the traces).

findings.claim: The exchange of first waves (their queen's loss to our knights minus ours to theirs in turns 20-50) is the single best early predictor of the race and accounts for about 45% of the margin difference, but its drivers are the opponent's tower count when our wave lands and whether both our groups are alive together - not our barracks timing, which is identical in lost and won races.
findings.numbers: DeathTrace, 180 games: their loss 20-50: 6.0 (lost races) vs 14.2 (won) (CI -12.1..-4.3); our loss 20-50: 10.5 vs 3.6; exchange -4.5 vs +10.7 (AUC 0.85); corr(final margin, exchange20_50) = 0.61 over 115 races (their loss alone 0.48, our loss alone 0.30). Mean margin lost -16.3 vs won +18.4 (34.7 HP apart): knight exchange in turns 0-50 accounts for 15.5 HP, 51-100 for 4.7, 101-end for 12.5, tower damage 2.0. Their loss by their towers at our first hit (180 games): 0 towers 43.3 HP (n=6), 1: 19.1 (85), 2: 9.4 (63), 3: 7.4 (11); 8 of our knights alive at t25 vs 1 tower: 23.3 (n=58), 4 knights vs 1 tower: 10.1 (27), vs 2 towers 9.4 either way. Our firstBarracks 9.17 vs 8.97 (p=0.63); our knights alive at t25 6.2 vs 6.0. Who hits first: in lost races their knights hit our queen first in 24 of 39 games where both hit; in won races ours hit first in 51 of 65 (our first hit median 28 vs 25.5; their first hit on us median 26.5 vs 36; 8/73 won races are never hit).
findings.evidence: q2_exchange.py -> q2-v12.txt; q7-v12.txt (towers at our hit x wave size). Observation (high confidence); the actionable share on our side is low.

findings.claim: A perfect first wave flips about a quarter of the lost races; a third of the lost races did not lose anything to the first wave.
findings.numbers: 42 lost races, final margins: 10 within 5 HP (four at -1), 18 within 10, median -13. Counterfactual lossK20 -> won mean 3.4 (rest of the game unchanged; ties go to seat 0): 10/42 flip; lossK20 -> 0: 13/42; lossK30 -> won mean: 10/42; 20-50 DeathTrace loss -> won mean: 10/42, -> 0: 14/42. Uniform HP gain: +2 flips 5, +5 flips 10, +10 flips 17, +15 flips 24 of 42. Symmetric risk: 20/73 won races would be lost if their lossK20 rose to the lost mean 10.2. Subgroups: one-tower lost races -> 2-tower mean: 8/24; 2nd tower at/after contact -> before-contact mean 2.0: 9/31; early-barracks opponents: 6/15. 14/42 lost races have lossK20 <= 3 (margins -2..-37): the first wave is irrelevant there. Deaths: lossK20 mean 9.4 (n=29), kills 8.2 (n=32). Rough rating value of 10 games of 180 = +5.6 pp win rate; with the Gold logistic scale 3.04 at p=0.61 that is about +0.7 rating points (3.04 x 0.056 / 0.238).
findings.evidence: q5_flip.py -> q5-v12.txt; q8-v12.txt section (2). Counterfactual inference: medium confidence for the flip counts, low for the rating conversion.

findings.claim: Lost races are against stronger opponents, and the second-tower timing matters most against them.
findings.numbers: Opponent rating at fetch: lost races 20.05 vs won 18.39 (CI +1.1..+2.3; AUC 0.75); race-loss share 24/39 (62%) vs opponents >=20, 18/76 (24%) vs <20; within >=20: lossK20 9.7 vs 3.3. All 176 games: opponent >=20 with our 2nd tower before the contact: won 11/19 (0.58), lossK20 4.3; at/after: 11/39 (0.28), lossK20 12.0; opponent <20: 46/62 (0.74) vs 37/56 (0.66). corr(2nd tower turn - contact, opp rating) = 0.21; corr(contact, opp rating) = -0.22. Won-race opponents trained more knights over the game (trainK 12.95 vs 10.95, p=0.011).
findings.evidence: q1-v12.txt (oppRating strata), q8-v12.txt section (3), manifests arena-6860036/6860166-games-2026-11-07.json. Observation; small n in the >=20 x before-contact cell.

findings.claim: v12 removed the distance effect v11 had and exposed the timing effect; the local panel exercises exactly the one-tower regime, and the rejected second-tower flags raised the tower count without raising tower HP, which is consistent with kill rate being the mechanism.
findings.numbers: v11 (171 games with contact, 44 lost / 62 won races): distance from the back edge at contact 444 vs 380 (CI +12..+116); towersAtContact 1.64 vs 1.73 (p=0.18); contact 27.9 vs 28.1 (p=0.37). v12: 322 vs 324 (p=0.89); towers 1.43 vs 1.75 (p=0.017); contact 24.5 vs 27.3 (p=0.021). Local first contacts (meet-back README profiles): mirror turn 24 with 1 tower, field 21 with 1, rival 25 with 1, boss 19 with 1. WAVE_TOWERS=2 / TOPUP_FROM=2 (exp-2026-11-05 README): contact with 2 towers, first-wave loss 7.3-8.2 vs 7.8 (no cut), summed tower HP at t50 1464/1436 vs 1648, queen deaths 36 vs 18 per 400 games.
findings.evidence: q1_compare.py v11 -> q1-v11.txt; W/docs/data/exp-2026-11-07-meet-back/README.md; W/docs/data/exp-2026-11-05-first-wave/README.md. Observation plus inference linking the local failure to the HP-driven damage formula; medium-high confidence.

levers.lever: Second tower up before the enemy's first wave arrives, WITHOUT starving the first tower: pump the first tower only to ~400-500 HP (2-3 turns instead of ~6 to 700) when a wave is coming, walk to the second site, then pump both; optionally triggered or tightened by the visible enemy barracks turn (<= 8 covers 42/180 games where we score 0.50).
levers.lossMode: HP race, first wave (also the vs-strong-opponents mode: within >=20-rated opponents the 2nd tower before the contact wins 11/19 vs 11/39 at/after)
levers.mechanism: Ladder order between the touch rule's top-up (TOWER_HP=700) and the next tower target: a conditional top-up threshold while towers < 2 and the WAVE_ANCHOR window is open (enemy knight barracks or knights visible). Tower damage is 3 + (range - dist)/200 per tower per turn with range from HP (Rules.java:355), so the aim is the summed damage rate at the contact (two towers of 450+700 beat one of 770 plus one of 196), not the count. This is a variant of the rejected WAVE_TOWERS/TOPUP_FROM family: those skipped ALL top-ups, left both towers at 200 HP (local tower HP at t50 1464 vs 1648) and doubled queen deaths; the new evidence is the t2rel gradient (lossK20 1.1 HP and 24% lost with the 2nd tower >=3 turns before the contact vs 11.6 HP and 63% lost >=3 turns after, n=21/27) and the kill-rate chain (ttk explains 43% of adjacent-turn variance).
levers.estimatedGain: Counterfactual on the arena games: 8 of the 24 one-tower lost races flip if their lossK20 fell to the 2-tower mean (9/31 for the 2nd-tower-after-contact subgroup), i.e. up to ~8-9 games of 180 (+4-5 pp) before costs; the symmetric exposure is 6 of 25 won one-tower races. Likely smaller in practice: the first tower's range at 450 HP is ~380 instead of ~500, and the old flags' failure shows deaths are the risk.
levers.measurability: Yes: mirror (contact turn 24, 1 tower), field (21, 1 tower) and rival (25, 1 tower) all meet the first wave in the one-tower regime; LocalProfile/WaveTrace can record the second tower turn minus the contact, the first-wave loss, summed tower HP at t50 and queen deaths per 1000 as tripwires (the 2026-11-05 flags doubled deaths against field).
levers.effort: flag on existing rule (conditional top-up threshold / ladder order); 1-2 parameters

levers.lever: Do not start a walk to a not-yet-built tower site while the wave is on her unless the site is within ~2 turns; instead hold at the existing tower and kite until the group is dead, then resume the ladder (a time-to-arrive/distance condition on the defence rule and ladder, not DEFENCE_FWD's half-plane).
levers.mechanism: The defence rule (threat with <2 towers within 500) and the ladder send the queen to the nearest free site; in lost races she walks 1.12 forward BUILD-new turns per game under knights (vs 0.30) at 1.7 HP per turn, and in the one-tower regime spends 2.9 walk turns to the 2nd site under knights (vs 1.7), the tower completing 3.5 vs 2.2 turns after the contact. The study's costliest traces (918150876, 918158655, 918146673, 918158658) show the walk through the knights and the stand at the 196-HP tower afterwards.
levers.estimatedGain: About 1-2 HP of the 6.8-HP gap (OLS: fwd BUILD-new 0.8 extra moves x ~1.7 HP; standing +1.0 HP); flips at most 2-5 of the 42 lost races on the uniform-gain table (+2 HP flips 5, +3 flips 6). Risk: THREAT_RADIUS=350 (fewer defence towers) lost 10 pp vs rival, so the tower must still be built, only later.
levers.measurability: Yes against mirror and field (both produce the defence walk at the contact); DEFENCE_FWD's failure (field -3 pp) is the reference; WaveTrace's walkTurnsToT2 / forward BUILD-new counts are the local metric.
levers.effort: flag on existing rule (defence rule / ladder gate by distance or turns to the site while a knight is within 250)

levers.lever: Record, do not pursue: standing within reach (STAND_REACH) and forward kiting penalties.
levers.mechanism: Standing turns with a knight within 155 are 0.52 vs 0.18 per game (~1 HP of the gap); forward moves while a knight is already adjacent cost the same as backward ones (1.31 vs 1.18 HP), and the kite's tower pull does not produce forward steps (0.12 vs 0.12 per game). STAND_REACH=155 and KITE_PULL=200 were already neutral locally.
levers.estimatedGain: <= 1 HP per lost race; 0-2 games of 180
levers.measurability: Already measured (STAND_REACH removes the standing turns without lowering the loss, mirror 7.9 vs 7.8)

levers.lever: The exchange of first waves is mostly the opponent's to decide (their tower count when our wave lands: 43 HP with 0 towers, 19 with 1, 9 with 2); the only our-side factor is whether both knight groups are alive together (8 knights vs 1 tower 23 HP, 4 knights 10 HP), which a single barracks cannot time (groups 5 turns apart). Not a cheap first-wave lever; hand to the army/midgame lens.
levers.lossMode: HP race, midgame (the 0-50 exchange is 45% of the margin gap but its drivers are theirs)
levers.mechanism: TRAIN timing with one barracks (first TRAIN at 80 gold at the barracks turn 9); our barracks timing is identical in lost and won races (9.17 vs 8.97), so no timing lever appears in the data.
levers.estimatedGain: unknown; the association (their loss 6.0 vs 14.2 HP) is driven by their builds
levers.measurability: field/rival build 1-2 towers early like Gold; the mirror's exchange is symmetric by construction
levers.effort: new rule at best; not recommended from this evidence

levers.lever: For the other lenses: 14 of the 42 lost races lost <= 3 HP to the first wave (margins -2 to -37) and the late-barracks opponents (first barracks >= 13, 82/180 games) cause 19 of the 29 queen deaths; neither is a first-wave problem.
levers.lossMode: HP race midgame / last 50 turns; queen death

caveats: All counterfactual flip counts hold the rest of the game fixed (a smaller first-wave loss would also change the opponent's later play and our top-up budget); the symmetric exposure (20/73 won races at the lost mean) shows the first wave is noisy both ways. Lost races are against stronger opponents (20.05 vs 18.39), who also build barracks earlier (corr of the 2nd-tower-minus-contact with rating 0.21), so part of the timing effect may be opponent quality; the within-rating strata are small (19 vs 39 games above 20). The kill-speed proxy sum(3 + hp//200) ignores range and the one-target rule (corr 0.68 with the recorded damage per turn; the recorded first-10-turn damage differs only 5.06 vs 5.59, p=0.06), so 'kill rate' is a mechanism inferred from the formula and the adjacency chain, not measured directly. The traces carry no knight positions: 'forward' means toward the enemy's edge, not toward the knights, and 'adjacent' uses the nearest-knight distance <= 60. Mann-Whitney p-values are normal approximations with tie correction over dozens of metrics; treat p between 0.02 and 0.10 as suggestive only; bootstrap CIs are percentile with 10000 resamples. summary.csv's spawned20 counts any enemy spawn in the window and is not the study's merged-wave definition; my merge definitions (net of kills: 17/42 vs 18/73; simple: 12/42 vs 12/73) bracket the README's 12 of 42. 176 of 180 games have a wave summary (the 2 referee-removed games and 2 kills lack a contact); the DeathTrace files cover all 180. Ties at equal HP were counted as a win on seat 0 and a loss on seat 1 (CG ranks player 0 first). The rating conversion (+0.7 points for 10 games) is a back-of-envelope logistic estimate with Gold's scale 3.04, not a measurement. Lever 1 is a variant of a twice-rejected family (WAVE_TOWERS/TOPUP_FROM); it is proposed only because the mechanism (tower HP -> damage rate -> adjacency) and the t2rel gradient are new, and its local test needs the death-rate tripwire. Confidence notes folded into the evidence fields: finding 2's association is high, its causal chain medium; finding 5 and finding 9 are medium-high; finding 7's rating conversion is low. No games were run; everything is from the recorded Gold replays' derived files.
